video_title: Can a Healthy Timberwolves Team Really Challenge the Spurs? | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves' defensive performance without Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: They have not only survived, they have thrived, and they have done it with one of the best defenses
quotes.quote: Let's talk about the Minnesota Timberwolves who I thought were going to fall off the proverbial cliff after Anthony Edwards went down with that knee injury. No way did I think they were going to survive without Anthony Edwards in that lineup. Well, they have not only survived, they have thrived, and they have done it with one of the best defenses in the NBA. They are number one, number two, or number three in a lot of defensive categories. They have been that good across the board on that end of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' team energy and defensive improvement
quotes.excerpt: I think one thing I make of the Timberwolves is just energy, just toughness.
quotes.quote: I think one thing I make of the Timberwolves is just energy, just toughness. They lost their star player and I feel like their camaraderie, they're all together, really, really believing in each other. You look at LaMelo Ball, you see them screaming out, I've never seen them play this much defense. I've never seen how he's been able to change, but also play at an All-Star level all while the guys have been out.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu's breakout season in Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: First full season in Minnesota, he's averaging 18 points per game.
quotes.quote: First full season in Minnesota, he's averaging 18 points per game.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaden McDaniels' evolution into a two-way player
quotes.excerpt: Jaden McDaniels is going from the conversation, 3-and-D to elite now, two-way scorer, two-way defender.
quotes.quote: Jaden McDaniels is going from the conversation, 3-and-D to elite now, two-way scorer, two-way defender because he's definitely dominating. Last night he put up 34 points, but he's scoring at will, he's scoring efficiently, and I just think they control the game. Those are tough kids, they're literally are with whatever, they're playing at a high level, they don't care, and I feel as though they know they're bad to the bone.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Dante DiVincenzo's recovery from Achilles injury
quotes.excerpt: If Dante DiVincenzo comes back from an Achilles tear after eight months, which is faster than Jason Tatum.
quotes.quote: If Dante DiVincenzo comes back from an Achilles tear after eight months, which is faster than Jason Tatum came back from his Achilles tear last year, we are really going to have to start looking at Achilles tears differently and how guys come back from it and just what the recovery time is going to be.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu's efficiency and shooting performance
quotes.excerpt: He's kind of flirting with those 50-40-90 numbers, which is a real testament to the efficiency.
quotes.quote: He's kind of flirting with those 50-40-90 numbers, which is a real testament to the efficiency of a player and he's well above 50% shooting and well above 40% from three-point range. So he's not just kind of passing those marks, he's been really good at that. His catch and shoot three-point numbers are outstanding as well.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Terrence Shannon Jr.'s impact off the bench
quotes.excerpt: Terrence Shannon Jr. has been great, legitimate guy, offensive weapon for this team coming off the bench.
quotes.quote: Terrence Shannon Jr. has been great, legitimate guy, offensive weapon for this team coming off the bench, double-digit scoring, I think it's in six consecutive games, 34 points against the Trail Blazers recently, gets to the free-throw line a lot. He's been really good for that team.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.excerpt: Jaden McDaniels, who they needed to take a step forward, he's done that as well.
quotes.quote: Jaden McDaniels, who they needed to take a step forward, he's done that as well. Against Brooklyn he had 34 points, 10 rebounds, six assists, he's been really good.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's role and potential with Anthony Edwards
quotes.excerpt: LaMelo's kind of the face of all this, but he's not playing great right now.
quotes.quote: LaMelo's kind of the face of all this, but he's not playing great right now. There's a lot better LaMelo Ball can play and will play when Anthony Edwards is back in the lineup. He's been a stabilizing force at the point guard position. We look at the offensive rating on-off, they're actually better with him off the court than they are with him on.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.excerpt: You can just feel the grittiness. They're not arrogant, but they're cocky.
quotes.quote: You can just feel the grittiness. They're not arrogant, but they're cocky. Literally they either going to blow you out or it could be a close game and it's going to be, you know what I mean, balls to the wall, like pelvis to pelvis, and I'm loving how they're playing.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing LaMelo Ball and Dylan Harper
quotes.excerpt: Anthony Edwards is the best player of let's say that collection of six guards between both teams.
quotes.quote: Anthony Edwards is the best player of let's say that collection of six guards between both teams. Is LaMelo better than Dylan Harper? I don't know. I don't know. He's flashier, but Dylan Harper is the goods, man.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's inconsistent performance with the Spurs
quotes.excerpt: He's had some inconsistent moments with the Spurs, don't you think?
quotes.quote: He's had some inconsistent moments with the Spurs, don't you think? Since stepping up, like that's all I'm saying, like it's I understand that three-headed rotation, but I always believe that it's all about what you're able to do and what you're able to take away and Timberwolves, they present a disruption factor, that's all I'm saying.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's shooting and performance analysis
quotes.excerpt: Stephon Castle's shooting percentage is down from last year by about four points.
quotes.quote: Stephon Castle's shooting percentage is down from last year by about four points, but his three-point percentage is up by about five points, his assists are right around where they were last year, turnovers are a little bit down. He's been fine. He's fine with them.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic as the MVP candidate
quotes.excerpt: I would make Luka the MVP, because of not only what he's put up offensively.
quotes.quote: Like as good as Luka Doncic has been, and I'm going to do this next week, but if you're talking like quarter-season awards, I would make Luka the MVP, because of not only what he's put up offensively, but how he's carried the Lakers to where they are right now. It's going to be really hard, not impossible, but really hard to hold off Victor Wembanyama, who is the most dominant defensive player we have ever seen.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's defensive dominance and impact
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama, who is the most dominant defensive player we have ever seen. Ever seen.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama, who is the most dominant defensive player we have ever seen. Ever seen. I include the great Bill Russell on that list. Will Chamberlain in his physicality on that list. Like what Wembanyama can do blocking shots, changing shots, discouraging people from even going to the basket. Like what he can do defensively is remarkable.
